C1.title: The scholarship shortcut
C1.tag: A scholarship offer with strings attached
C1.brief: Anaya has brought a fictional phone to the kiosk. Inspect the conversations, identify the pressure tactics, and rebuild what happened. No real money is used.
C1.closing: Case closed. You checked the evidence, named the tactics, and chose a safer response.
C1.debrief.mechanism: The sender creates a story, adds pressure, discourages outside checks, and asks for money or account access.
C1.debrief.c1: Pause before responding to a message that creates pressure.
C1.debrief.c2: Verify the claim through a contact you find independently.
C1.debrief.c3: Protect your payment details and ask a trusted person for help.

C1.fix.q: What is the safest next step?
C1.fix.safe: Stop the conversation, verify independently, and ask a trusted person for help.
C1.fix.safe.why: This removes the pressure and gives you a reliable way to check the request.
C1.fix.pay: Send the money first and check later.
C1.fix.pay.why: Sending money first gives the sender what they want before the claim is verified.
C1.fix.share: Share the requested account details to settle the matter.
C1.fix.share.why: Account secrets and device access should stay private, regardless of the story.
C1.replay.1: The sender starts a story to attract attention.
C1.replay.2: A claimed identity or frightening statement makes the story feel important.
C1.replay.3: A deadline creates pressure to act.
C1.replay.5: The sender asks for money, secrets, or control of the device.
